LESSON: READING 10.2.1 NOTE MAKING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.2: Reading 10.2.1 Note Making

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 10.2.1 Note Making. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: what situations could notes be made?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify main points or ideas in an argumentative passage

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify main points or ideas in an argumentative passage
   In simple words: practise until you can identify main points or ideas in an argumentative passage. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 10.2.1 Note Making using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 10.2.1 Note Making in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 10.2.1 Note Making to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 10.2.1 Note Making.
4. Show that you can: identify main points or ideas in an argumentative passage

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 10.2.1 Note Making using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 10.2.1 Note Making important for a Grade 9 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Practise, in groups, the note-making procedures such as sq4r, read argumentative passages based on the theme of social and mass media,
2. Graphically prepare charts using their notes,
3. Learning to learn: It occurs as the learner reads and makes notes on argumentative passages.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. what situations could notes be made?
2. Why is it important to make notes?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify main points or ideas in an argumentative passage

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
